Subject: Post-incident evidence preservation — Greenfield Health

Hi Sam,

Thanks again for the quick sync this morning. Per our call, I wanted to confirm Redwood's intended approach to preserving forensic evidence from the incident you reported (customer-facing app error leading to suspected data access). Please confirm if Greenfield has any additional constraints, but our current plan is: 

- Immediate snapshot of S3 buckets and KVS prefixes implicated in the incident (immutable copy)
- Export of CloudTrail and control-plane audit logs for the 48-hour window around the event
- Capture of runtime KV cache state + model-only artifacts (no customer payload extraction unless requested)
- Chain-of-custody PDF to be signed by both parties

Questions for you:
1) Do you want us to push the bundles to your forensics vendor (CyberFirm) SFTP endpoint, or would you prefer a shared Drive link with restricted access?
2) Any legal hold or extended retention requirement beyond standard 90 days? We can extend preserved evidence to 1 year for escalations.

Attachments: none in this message.

Next steps: If you confirm SFTP, we'll prepare an encrypted tarball and provide key-exchange notes to CyberFirm. If you prefer Drive, we'll provision a locked folder and share it to forensics@cyberfirm.io.

Regards,

Soojin Lee
Manager, Incident Response
Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-incident evidence preservation — Greenfield Health

Soojin / team,

Quick technical confirmation on retention and export mechanics: 

- Current platform defaults: object logs (S3) retained 90 days; control-plane audit trails retained 180 days.
- Forensics export: we will create an immutable S3 prefix with versioning and an object lock in governance mode (retention until 2028-03-21 by default if you ask for 1 yr).
- CloudTrail: we will copy the relevant eventset to a dedicated account bucket with KMS key rotation disabled for the export period. The exported bucket will be encrypted with a customer-shared KMS key (we can generate and share a CMK ARN or use your provided key).
- PSI / sensitive payloads: our policy is to avoid extracting customer PII into packets unless Greenfield requests it in writing. We will instead provide hashes, timestamps, request IDs, and the platform-level access logs necessary to correlate activity.

Chain of custody practices: we will generate a PDF log that records the snapshot operation, operator, UTC timestamp, and SHA256 checksums for each artefact. If Greenfield requires notarization, we can escalate to legal.

Hold windows we recommend for incidents that may involve regulatory review: 365 days for evidence repositories, expandable by legal request. For day-to-day postmortems, 90 days is typical.

Action items for us:
- Prepare immutable export and a tar.gz with prescribed manifest
- Place export in restricted Drive AND start SFTP upload if Sam requests SFTP
- Create chain_of_custody-form.docx and pre-populate with snapshot metadata

I'll start the export run at 13:00 PT and post the link here once complete.

-Vivek
Principal Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Sam Greenfield <sam.greenfield@greenfieldhealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: CyberFirm Forensics <forensics@cyberfirm.io>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 08:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-incident evidence preservation — Greenfield Health

Thanks Soojin and Vivek — that plan sounds good. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- CyberFirm prefers SFTP for large bundles; their endpoint is sftp.cyberfirm.io:8022 and they will handle checksum verification.
- We will need the export to include the original request IDs and full CloudTrail event JSONs (they will run parsing on their side). If there are any legal constraints on providing full event payloads, flag them and we'll coordinate with legal.
- We will sign chain_of_custody on our end as well; please send the pre-filled doc.

Please confirm ETA for the SFTP upload and whether you will use our KMS key or Redwood's temporary key.

-Sam
Head of Security
Greenfield Health

Sam — thanks, confirmed. Summary of agreed steps and ETA below (will also drop these into HubSpot GH-4683):

1) Export run completed at 11:12 PT. Artefacts created: log-bundle-20270321.tar.gz (S3 prefix: s3://evidence-exports/greenfield/2027-03-21/), manifest and SHA256 sums, chain_of_custody-form.docx (pre-populated).
2) Upload method: SFTP to sftp.cyberfirm.io:8022 — scheduled for 13:00 PT. We will use your KMS key if you provide the ARN by 12:30 PT; otherwise we will encrypt with a temporary Redwood CMK and provide the key exchange artifacts.
3) Payload scope: full CloudTrail JSONs (control-plane), application request IDs, request headers (no decrypted customer PII blobs extracted). If CyberFirm requires additional information, please outline the exact fields.
4) Retention: export will be object-locked for 365 days by default; we will not enable automatic lifecycle deletion during that window.

Attachments: forensic-handoff-checklist.pdf; log-bundle-20270321.tar.gz (attachment stub).

Link to Drive archive (read-only): https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2B3cForensicDrive
HubSpot: GH-4683

If you confirm the KMS ARN, we'll proceed with your key. Otherwise scheduled upload will use Redwood's CMK and we will provide the KMS-wrapped key exchange file via the Drive link.

Best,

Soojin Lee
